teacherNotes.title: Core Words
teacherNotes.content: tall, short, young, old, hair, eyes, brown, blue, green, dark, fair, handsome, beautiful

elements.content: Core Active Vocabulary (10-20 items):
tall, short, young, old, hair, eyes, brown, blue, green, dark, fair, handsome, beautiful
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• What does he look like? (asking appearance)
• She has brown hair and green eyes (describing features)
• He is tall and handsome (describing build & look)
• They look similar (comparing appearance)
Pronunciation Focus:
Pronunciation of vowel sounds in 'tall' /tɔːl/, 'eyes' /aɪz/, 'fair' /feə/.

teacherNotes.title: Grammar Function
teacherNotes.content: Adjective order and verbs 'be' vs 'have got' for features (He is tall, She has blue eyes)

elements.content: Grammar System & Functional Framing:
Adjective order and verbs 'be' vs 'have got' for features (He is tall, She has blue eyes)
Controlled Practice:
He is 190 cm tall and not short. How do you describe him?
Reading Script & Dialogue:

A: What does your brother look like?
B: He is tall and thin. He has short dark hair and brown eyes.
A: Is he similar to your father?
B: Yes, they look very similar.
Listen to two friends talking about family photos and identify who is being described.

teacherNotes.title: Speaking Aim (~70%)
teacherNotes.content: Practice speaking with your partner: I can describe the physical appearance of family members and friends.
